use_cases.label: Get a patient's records for treatment
use_cases.summary: Ways a clinician can pull a patient's records from other organizations when treating them.

use_cases.label: Get my own records (as a patient)
use_cases.summary: Ways a patient can get their own records, through a portal, an app or a request.

use_cases.label: Find a provider's endpoint
use_cases.summary: Ways to find the electronic address where a provider or organization receives data.

use_cases.label: Exchange data with a payer (patient access, provider access, payer-to-payer, prior authorization)
use_cases.summary: Ways data moves between payers, patients and providers under the CMS interoperability rules.

use_cases.label: Get admit and discharge alerts
use_cases.summary: Ways to be notified when a patient is admitted to or discharged from a hospital or emergency department.

use_cases.label: Report to public health
use_cases.summary: Ways to send reportable conditions, immunizations and lab results to public health agencies.

use_cases.label: Refer someone to a community organization
use_cases.summary: Ways to refer a person to a social service or community organization and track the outcome.

glossary.definition: Health information exchange: an organization or network that moves patient health data between providers and other authorized parties.
Qualified Health Information Network: an organization designated under TEFCA to connect participants and route queries between networks.
Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement: the federal framework that sets common rules for nationwide health information exchange.
A secure messaging standard for sending health information from one address to another, similar to encrypted email between providers.
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: the HL7 standard for exchanging health data over web APIs.
Integrating the Healthcare Enterprise: a body that publishes profiles for how systems exchange data, such as document sharing and patient lookup.
Admit, discharge and transfer: the messages a hospital sends when a patient arrives, leaves or moves.
National Directory of Healthcare: the HL7 FHIR implementation guide that describes how providers, organizations and endpoints are listed in a directory.
The electronic address, usually a web URL or a Direct address, where an organization receives or serves health data.
